articles.title: Senado do Paraguai suspende votação de renúncia de presidente | G1
articles.standfirst: Presidente apresentou renúncia após quebra do banco ueno, que deixou milhões de clientes sem acesso a depósitos; deputados aprovaram acusação contra Peña por suspeita de conflito de interesses.
articles.summary: Presidente apresentou renúncia após quebra do banco ueno, que deixou milhões de clientes sem acesso a depósitos; deputados aprovaram acusação contra Peña por suspeita de conflito de interesses.
articles.body:
O Congresso do Paraguai interrompeu nesta quinta-feira (5) a sessão que decidiria sobre a renúncia do presidente Santiago Peña . O país vive uma profunda crise política após vir a tona um escândalo envolvendo a quebra do banco ueno, que deixou milhões de clientes sem acesso a seus depósitos.

A votação foi suspensa depois que parlamentares do Partido Colorado, partido de Peña, deixaram o plenário, derrubando assim o quórum necessário para a continuidade da sessão. Com isso, a renúncia não foi aceita, e Peña continua no cargo.

Senadores disseram à TV paraguaia ABC Color que a sessão será retomada na sexta-feira (5) , já com a pauta do impeachment.

A saída dos parlamentares ocorreu após um longo debate entre governistas e oposicionistas sobre o futuro do presidente. Quando perceberam que não tinham votos suficientes para aprovar a renúncia, os integrantes da base governista abandonaram a sessão, que acabou encerrada.

Veja, abaixo, a cronologia da crise no país vizinho:

Na manhã desta quinta (5), o Congresso do Paraguai deu os primeiros passos para votar um impeachment contra Santiago Peña , e contra seu vice, Pedro Alliana;

Horas depois, Peña apresentou uma carta de renúncia ;

A Câmara do Paraguai , no entanto, não aceitou a renúncia e decidiu dar seguimento do processo de impeachment contra Peña - a votação foi unânime;

Já o processo de impeachment contra o vice, Pedro Alliana, foi rejeitado . A decisão abriu caminho para Alliana assumir a presidência do país.

Durante a tarde, o Senado abriu uma sessão para julgar o pedido de renúncia do presidente Peña, mas a sessão foi suspensa por falta de quórum. Com isso, o presidente continua no cargo.

Segundo senadores presentes na sessão, o Senado deve retomar na sexta-feira (6) a análise do processo de impeachment contra Peña.

Em carta publicada na noite desta quinta, Peña disse que vai se apresentar para fazer sua defesa no processo do impeachment.

No início da tarde, a Câmara dos Deputados aprovou por unanimidade, com 78 votos, a abertura do processo de impeachment contra Santiago Peña . Na sessão conjunta do Congresso, porém, foi colocada em votação o pedido de renúncia do presidente.

A oposição defendia que o Congresso rejeitasse a renúncia e desse continuidade ao impeachment . Os parlamentares argumentavam que a saída voluntária permitiria a Peña assumir uma vaga de senador vitalício, com direito a foro privilegiado.

➡️ No Paraguai , ex-presidentes que concluíram seus mandatos ou renunciaram ao cargo ganham o título de senador vitalício, o que lhe garante imunidade parlamentar pelo restante da vida.

O senador de oposição Líder Amarilla alegou que aceitar a renúncia poderia impedir que o presidente respondesse a eventuais acusações na Justiça.

"Se aceitarmos esta renúncia, o que estamos fazendo é permitir que Santiago Peña obtenha foro parlamentar e que todo o dinheiro que foi roubado fique impune, porque a Promotoria não poderá apresentar acusações contra ele", disse Amarilla, em entrevista ao ABC Color.

Já os governistas sustentavam que aceitar a saída do presidente seria a maneira mais rápida de encerrar a crise política e permitir a transferência de poder ao vice-presidente, Pedro Alliana.

O grupo também afirmava que o Senado poderia analisar um eventual pedido de retirada do foro de Peña, caso a Promotoria solicitasse a medida.

Com a interrupção da sessão, a renúncia de Peña continua sem uma decisão formal do Congresso. O processo de impeachment, aprovado pela Câmara dos Deputados mais cedo, permanece em aberto e deverá seguir para análise do Senado, responsável pelo julgamento do presidente .

Entenda os últimos acontecimento da crise

Segundo Ariel Palacios, comentarista da GloboNews e especialista em América Latina, Peña tentou se blindar e manter seu foro privilegiado ao anunciar sua decisão de renunciar. Isso porque, pela Constituição do Paraguai , ao deixar o cargo, os ex-presidentes da República viram senadores vitalícios.

A manobra, no entanto, foi frustrada quando a Câmara deu seguimento à abertura do impeachment. A Carta constitucional estabelece que o ex-presidente perde essa prerrogativa se tiver sido submetido a julgamento político e for considerado culpado.

Opositores advertiram que aceitar a renúncia permitiria a Peña ter uma blindagem parlamentar, impedindo que fosse julgado pela Justiça comum pelas suspeitas de crimes relacionados à crise do banco ueno.

👉 A Constituição paraguaia estabelece que é prerrogativa do Congresso aceitar ou rejeitar a renúncia do presidente da República e a do vice-presidente.

Santiago Penã apresentou sua carta de renúncia em um vídeo , em que se desculpou com a população que perdeu o acesso ao próprio dinheiro e disse que decidiu renunciar "pensando na estabilidade do nosso país, na paz social e na necessidade de preservar nossas instituições democráticas".

"Estou convencido de que nenhum cargo pode estar acima do bem-estar do Paraguai . Também quero pedir desculpas ao povo. Se em algum momento falhei, nunca foi minha intenção decepcionar a confiança que depositaram em mim", disse.

➡️ Santiago Peña é alvo de críticas por conta da crise bancária que começou após o banco digital ueno fechar as portas e deixar milhares de clientes sem acesso ao próprio dinheiro . Peña foi acionista do grupo que controla a instituição, e a oposição acusa o Banco Central paraguaio de encobrir irregularidades ( leia mais abaixo ).

Santiago Peña, economista e ex-ministro da Fazenda durante o governo de Cartes, é o atual candidato presidencial do Colorado — Foto: REUTERS

Clientes do banco ueno fazem protesto em Assunção, no Paraguai, em 5 de novembro de 2026. — Foto: Daniel Duarte/ AFP

“Nunca antes alguém prejudicou, em um único dia, 3 milhões de pessoas na República do Paraguai , e o senhor conseguiu isso, senhor presidente... o senhor é a origem desse monstro que criou”, disse a deputada de oposição Rocío Vallejo durante a sessão, pouco antes da apresentação do pedido.

A acusação foi apresentada por 35 deputados, que pediram ao presidente da Câmara a convocação da sessão extraordinária.

Penã foi acionista do grupo dono do banco

Deputado da oposição no Paraguai segura cartaz em ato que pede impeachment do presidente Santiago Peña após fechamento de banco virtual que gerou crise bancária no país, em 5 de novembro de 2026. — Foto: Cesar Olmedo/ Reuters

👉 Peña, que também é economista, foi acionista do grupo proprietário do ueno até março do ano passado . O banco tinha cerca de 3 milhões de clientes e concentrava aproximadamente US$ 850 milhões em depósitos públicos, incluindo recursos do Instituto de Previdência Social.

O ueno, que pertence ao Grupo Vázquez, fechou as portas na terça-feira (3), depois que o Banco Central iniciou sua liquidação. A autoridade monetária identificou uma insuficiência de recursos para cobrir as obrigações do banco, relacionada a empréstimos concedidos a empresas vinculadas à instituição.

Em uma publicação em suas redes sociais, o presidente paraguaio afirmou que os responsáveis pelas irregularidades responderão à Justiça , sem exceções. A declaração foi feita pouco antes de que ele promulgasse uma lei que permitirá aos clientes do ueno recuperar seu dinheiro mais rapidamente.

“Peço veementemente a todos os setores políticos que coloquem o interesse dos poupadores acima de qualquer outro interesse”, afirmou.

Executivos do ueno se entregaram às autoridades após a emissão de mandados de prisão pela Procuradoria, que também acusou formalmente 27 pessoas ligadas ao banco. A Justiça ordenou ainda o bloqueio dos bens dos acusados.

Nesta quarta-feira, também circularam relatos de falhas em aplicativos de outros bancos, o que aumentou a preocupação com o sistema financeiro do país.

A Associação de Bancos do Paraguai (Asoban) informou que as instituições financeiras trabalhavam para atender ao grande volume de clientes que estavam transferindo suas contas do ueno. A entidade ressaltou que o sistema bancário continuava “operando normalmente”.

Pessoas fazem fila para tentar retirar dinheiro em banco em Assunção, no Paraguai, diante de temor gerado por crise bancária no país, em 3 de novembro de 2026. — Foto: Daniel Duarte/ AFP

articles.title: Santiago Peña renuncia no Paraguai e garante foro como senador | G1
articles.standfirst: Constituição do Paraguai prevê que ex-presidentes tenham cargo de senador vitalício e, consequentemente, foro privilegiado até o fim da vida. Porém apenas para aqueles que não tenham sido considerados culpados em julgamentos políticos.
articles.summary: Segundo Ariel Palácios, o agora ex-presidente paraguaio tomou a decisão para se blindar e "evitar ter que ir à Justiça por conta do escândalo financeiro" ligado ao banco Ueno.
articles.body:
O presidente do Paraguai , Santiago Peña, tentou se blindar e manter seu foro privilegiado ao anunciar sua decisão de renunciar nesta quinta-feira (5) , afirma Ariel Palácios.

De acordo com o comentarista da GloboNews, especialista em América Latina, o agora ex-presidente paraguaio decidiu pela renúncia para evitar enfrentar um processo na Justiça e ser investigado pelo escândalo financeiro ligado ao fechamento do banco digital ueno.

Isso porque, pela Constituição do país, ao deixar o cargo, os ex-presidentes da República viram senadores vitalícios e, consequentemente, foro privilegiado até o fim da vida . Podem participar das sessões e comissões, mas não votam e não contam para quórum.

No entanto, "se tiverem sido submetidos a julgamento político e considerados culpados", eles perdem esse privilégio . Peña corre esse risco, já que, mais cedo, o Congresso do país tomou os primeiros passos para votar um impeachment contra ele e seu vice .

"Com esta renúncia, Peña evita o impeachment e consegue foro privilegiado. Isso porque, no Paraguai - único caso em toda a América do Sul -, quando termina o mandato de um presidente - eles não podem ser reeleitos -, automaticamente eles recebem de presente o cargo de senador vitalício. A pessoa tem foro privilegiado até falecer. Então, Santiago Peña com isso se blindaria para evitar ter que ir à Justiça por conta desse escândalo financeiro", explica Ariel.

Pouco depois do anúncio, a tentativa de Peña foi frustrada. A Câmara de Deputados do Paraguai aprovou dar seguimento a seu processo de impeachment e rejeitou a carta de renúncia apresentada por ele.

Opositores advertiram que aceitar a renúncia permitiria a Peña ter uma blindagem parlamentar, impedindo que fosse julgado pela Justiça comum pelas suspeitas de crimes relacionados ao esquema do banco ueno.

Santiago Peña, presidente do Paraguai desde 2023 que renunciou ao cargo em 5 de novembro de 2026. — Foto: REUTERS/Cesar Olmedo/File Photo

Peña renunciou à Presidência da República do Paraguai no começo da tarde desta quinta. Alvo de um processo de impeachment que havia angariado o apoio tanto da oposição quanto da base governista, ele anunciou sua decisão nas redes sociais.

No vídeo - veja a íntegra aqui -, ele se desculpou com a população afetada pela crise bancária e disse que decidiu renunciar "pensando na estabilidade do nosso país, na paz social e na necessidade de preservar nossas instituições democráticas".

"Estou convencido de que nenhum cargo pode estar acima do bem-estar do Paraguai . Também quero pedir desculpas ao povo. Se em algum momento falhei, nunca foi minha intenção decepcionar a confiança que depositaram em mim", disse.

Pessoas fazem fila para tentar retirar dinheiro em banco em Assunção, no Paraguai, diante de temor gerado por crise bancária no país, em 3 de novembro de 2026. — Foto: Daniel Duarte/ AFP

Santiago Peña, era alvo de críticas por conta da crise bancária que começou após o banco digital Ueno fechar as portas e deixar milhares de clientes sem acesso ao próprio dinheiro . Ele foi acionista do grupo que controla a instituição, e a oposição acusa o Banco Central paraguaio de encobrir irregularidades ( leia mais abaixo ).

Nesta manhã, o Congresso do Paraguai iniciou uma sessão extraordinária para debater o pedido de impeachment, e todas as bancadas da Câmara dos Deputados anunciaram que votariam a favor do impeachment .

A sessão foi o primeiro passo do processo , que ganhou força após o Horário Cortes, atual presidente do Partido Colorado, sigla de Peña, retirar o apoio ao governo.

Economista conservador, Santiago Peña assumiu o governo do Paraguai em 2023 e seu mandato duraria até 2028. Seu vice, Pedro Alliana, assume o poder , mas ele também é alvo do processo de impeachment.

articles.title: Congresso do Paraguai aprova votar impeachment de Santiago Peña | G1
articles.standfirst: Mais cedo, Santiago Peña apresentou carta de renúncia. Deputados rejetiram a renúncia e decidiram votar impeachment. Peña é acusado de ser conivente com crise bancária após banco virtual do qual foi acionista fechar e deixar milhares de clientes sem seu dinheiro.
articles.summary: A Câmara de Deputados do Paraguai aprovou nesta quinta-feira (5) dar seguimento do processo de impeachment de  Santiago Peña.
articles.body:
A Câmara de Deputados do Paraguai aprovou nesta quinta-feira (5) dar seguimento do processo de impeachment do presidente do país, Santiago Peña .

Os deputados também rejeitaram a carta de renúncia apresentada por Peña — a Constituição paraguaia estabelece que é prerrogativa do Congresso aceitar ou rejeitar a renúncia do presidente da República e a do vice-presidente.

Mais cedo, ele havia renunciado ao cargo, em meio à crise bancária do país ( leia mais abaixo ).

Os deputados aprovaram por unanimidade a abertura do processo de impeachment após forte pressão da oposição, com o intuito de evitar que Peña mantivesse o foro privilegiado.

👉 Isso porque o artigo 189 da Constituição paraguaia garante um cargo vitalício de senador , sem poder de voto, mas com a garantia de imunidade parlamentar. Esse cargo, no entanto, é cancelado no caso de o presidente sofrer impeachment .

A oposição acredita, portanto, que a renúncia foi uma manobra de Peña para evitar o impeachment e, com isso, manter a imunidade parlamentar.

Antes de aprovar seguir com o processo de Peña, os deputados paraguaios rejeitaram abrir um processo de impeachment também para seu vice , Pedro Alliana, pedindo pela oposição. A rejeição blinda o vice-presidente abre caminho para que Alliana assuma a presidência do país.

Ele deve assumir o cargo ainda nesta quinta-feira, durante uma sessão extraordinária da Câmara e do Senado, em que os legisladores devem votar o impeachment de Santigo Peña.

O presidente paraguaio anunciou sua renúncia nesta quinta-feira após ficar isolado por conta da crise bancário. Ele é acusado pela oposição de ter sido conivente com a quebra do banco digital Ueno, que bloqueou a conta de milhares de correntistas e do qual o presidente foi acionista ( leia mais abaixo ).

Em um vídeo , o presidente se desculpou com a população que perdeu o acesso ao próprio dinheiro e disse que decidiu renunciar "pensando na estabilidade do nosso país, na paz social e na necessidade de preservar nossas instituições democráticas".

"Estou convencido de que nenhum cargo pode estar acima do bem-estar do Paraguai . Também quero pedir desculpas ao povo. Se em algum momento falhei, nunca foi minha intenção decepcionar a confiança que depositaram em mim", disse.

Santiago Penã anuncia renúncia — Foto: Reprodução/X

Nesta manhã, o Congresso do Paraguai havia inciado uma sessão extraordinária para debater o pedido de impeachment, e todas as bancadas da Câmara dos Deputados anunciaram que votariam a favor do impeachment .

A iniciativa que ganhou força após o Horário Cortes, atual presidente do Partido Colorado, sigla de Peña, retirar o apoio ao governo. Cortes é considerado o mentor de Peña. O presidente do Congresso, Basilio Nuñez, do Partido Colorado, também havia retirado apoio.

Economista conservador, Santiago Peña assumiu o governo do Paraguai em 2023 e seu mandato duraria até 2028. Seu vice, Pedro Alliana, assume o poder , mas ele também é alvo do processo de impeachment.

Peña era aliado do presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, e integrava o Escudo das Américas , grupo de presidentes de países da América Latina ideologicamente alinhados a Trump. No entanto, Peña também tinha boa relação com o presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva.

CLIENTES DE BANCO SEM DINHEIRO: entenda a crise bancária que levou à renúncia

Santiago Peña, economista e ex-ministro da Fazenda durante o governo de Cartes, é o atual candidato presidencial do Colorado — Foto: REUTERS

Clientes do banco Ueno fazem protesto em Assunção, no Paraguai, em 5 de novembro de 2026. — Foto: Daniel Duarte/ AFP

👉 Santiago Peña , que também é economista, foi acionista do grupo proprietário do Ueno até março do ano passado . O banco tinha cerca de 3 milhões de clientes e concentrava aproximadamente US$ 850 milhões em depósitos públicos, incluindo recursos do Instituto de Previdência Social.

Deputado da oposição no Paraguai segura cartaz em ato que pede impeachment do presidente Santiago Peña após fechamento de banco virtual que gerou crise bancária no país, em 5 de novembro de 2026. — Foto: Cesar Olmedo/ Reuters

O Ueno, que pertence ao Grupo Vázquez, fechou as portas na terça-feira (3), depois que o banco central iniciou sua liquidação. A autoridade monetária identificou uma insuficiência de recursos para cobrir as obrigações do banco, relacionada a empréstimos concedidos a empresas vinculadas à instituição.

Em uma publicação em suas redes sociais, o presidente paraguaio afirmou que os responsáveis pelas irregularidades responderão à Justiça , sem exceções. A declaração foi feita pouco antes de que ele promulgasse uma lei que permitirá aos clientes do Ueno recuperar seu dinheiro mais rapidamente.

“Peço veementemente a todos os setores políticos que coloquem o interesse dos poupadores acima de qualquer outro interesse”, afirmou.

Pessoas fazem fila para tentar retirar dinheiro em banco em Assunção, no Paraguai, diante de temor gerado por crise bancária no país, em 3 de novembro de 2026. — Foto: Daniel Duarte/ AFP

Executivos do Ueno se entregaram às autoridades após a emissão de mandados de prisão pela Procuradoria, que também acusou formalmente 27 pessoas ligadas ao banco. A Justiça ordenou ainda o bloqueio dos bens dos acusados.

Na quarta-feira (4), também circularam relatos de falhas em aplicativos de outros bancos, o que aumentou a preocupação com o sistema financeiro do país.

A Associação de Bancos do Paraguai (Asoban) informou que as instituições financeiras trabalhavam para atender ao grande volume de clientes que estavam transferindo suas contas do Ueno. A entidade ressaltou que o sistema bancário continuava “operando normalmente”.

articles.title: IBGE abre 513 vagas de recenseador no Leste e Nordeste de MG | G1
articles.standfirst: Inscrições vão até 25 de novembro. Remuneração pode chegar a R$ 4.370 por mês, conforme a produtividade.
articles.summary: Inscrições começam nesta sexta-feira (6) e vão até 25 de novembro. Veja os requisitos e saiba como participar da seleção.
articles.body:
Começam nesta sexta-feira (6) as inscrições para o processo seletivo temporário do IBGE, que oferece 513 vagas de recenseador em cidades do Leste e Nordeste de Minas Gerais. O prazo vai até 25 de novembro.

Ao todo, o edital prevê 27.279 vagas no país, sendo 2.884 em Minas Gerais.

Para concorrer, é necessário ter ensino fundamental completo e mais de 18 anos no momento da contratação. A jornada de trabalho é de 40 horas semanais.

A remuneração fixa é de R$ 1.741 por mês, acrescida de uma parcela variável calculada conforme a produtividade. Essa parcela pode chegar a R$ 2.629, elevando a remuneração mensal a até R$ 4.370.

Entre os benefícios previstos estão auxílio-alimentação de R$ 1.192 e ajuda para custear os deslocamentos necessários ao trabalho.

Distribuição das vagas por cidade ou área

Nanuque e Serra dos Aimorés , em área conjunta

Coronel Fabriciano e Timóteo, em área conjunta

Frei Inocêncio e Mathias Lobato, em área conjunta

Nacip Raydan e São José da Safira, em área conjunta

Os interessados devem fazer a inscrição no site da comissã organizadora até 25 de novembro. A taxa é de R$ 70. Pessoas de baixa renda que atendam aos critérios do edital e doadores de medula óssea cadastrados no Redome podem solicitar isenção.

A seleção será feita por prova objetiva, prevista para 31 de janeiro de 2027. Serão 60 questões: 15 de Língua Portuguesa, 15 de Matemática e 30 de conhecimentos técnicos.

articles.title: Ministério da Agricultura investiga doença contagiosa em ave  | G1
articles.standfirst: Animal da espécie pato-do-mato (Cairina moschata) foi registrado em Guarujá (SP).
articles.summary: O Ministério da Agricultura investiga ave em Guarujá com suspeita de influenza aviária ou doença de Newcastle.
articles.body:
Ministério da Agricultura e Pecuária investiga síndrome respiratória em ave encontrada em Guarujá, SP — Foto: Reprodução/Mapa e Michiel de Groot/iNaturalist

O Ministério da Agricultura e Pecuária (Mapa) investiga um caso de suspeita de síndrome respiratória em uma ave silvestre encontrada em Guarujá , no litoral de São Paulo. O animal da espécie pato-do-mato (Cairina moschata) foi registrado no bairro Sítio Conceiçãozinha.

As doenças-alvo da investigação são a influenza aviária e a doença de Newcastle . De acordo com o Mapa, elas são virais e contagiosas, sendo obrigatória a notificação à Organização Mundial de Saúde Animal (OMSA). Além das aves, também podem afetar répteis, mamíferos e até seres humanos.

Segundo o ministério, a ave encontrada em Guarujá foi classificada por um médico veterinário como um caso provável de Síndrome Respiratória e Nervosa. O Mapa aguarda um resultado laboratorial conclusivo das amostras que foram coletadas.

Conforme divulgado pelo Museu Nacional, o pato-do-mato ocorre em brejos e rios da América do Sul. Essa espécie foi modificada pelo homem, dando origem ao chamado pato-doméstico. Apesar de ser pesada, ela tem grande poder de voo e executa movimentos migratórios.

O g1 questionou o ministério sobre como tem sido feito o acompanhamento da ave registrada no litoral de São Paulo, mas não obteve retorno até a última atualização desta reportagem.

O ministério destacou que a influenza aviária é uma doença de distribuição mundial, com ciclos pandêmicos ao longo dos anos, e com graves consequências ao comércio internacional de produtos avícolas. Em 2023, ela foi detectada pela primeira vez em território nacional, diagnosticada em aves silvestres, o que não compromete a condição do Brasil como país livre de IAAP para o comércio.

A doença de Newcastle foi considerada erradicada no país em 2006. Após esse período, somente em 17 de julho de 2024, foi novamente confirmado um foco no país, em um estabelecimento avícola comercial de frango de corte, no estado do Rio Grande do Sul, imediatamente notificado à OMSA.

Em 18 de outubro de 2026, foi confirmado novo foco da doença, em estabelecimento avícola comercial de perus de corte, localizado no estado de Santa Catarina, igualmente notificado de forma imediata à OMSA.

articles.title: They promised Afghan women freedom, delivered bans: Inside five years of Taliban rule
articles.summary: They promised girls the right to study up to university level, women the freedom to work and an Afghanistan where their rights would be protected.
articles.body: They promised girls the right to study up to university level, women the freedom to work and an Afghanistan where their rights would be protected.Five years after returning to power, the Taliban's promises lie in stark contrast with the reality. More than 2.6 million adolescent girls have been denied secondary education since 2021, women remain barred from universities, and 53 per cent of Afghanistan's primary school-age children are now outside formal education.A joint report by UNESCO and UNICEF, titled Afghanistan Education Situation Report 2026, raised concerns over the deteriorating quality of education in the country. Citing a national assessment of more than 55,000 Grade 4 students across all 34 provinces, the report found that fewer than half had achieved minimum proficiency in language at the Grade 3 level, while only one in four met the corresponding proficiency level in mathematics.It further found that fewer than one in 100 children aged three to four participate in early childhood education programmes.The Taliban's return to power came amid the withdrawal of US and Nato forces after nearly 20 years of military presence in Afghanistan.The withdrawal followed the February 2020 Doha Agreement, signed between the Trump administration and the Taliban, under which Washington committed to withdrawing its forces in exchange for security commitments from the group and its pledge to engage in intra-Afghan negotiations.As foreign forces withdrew, the Taliban launched a rapid offensive, capturing provincial capitals before entering Kabul on August 15, 2021, as then-president Ashraf Ghani fled the country. The US completed its military withdrawal on August 30, 2021.What the Taliban promised Afghan women and what they got insteadJust two days after capturing Kabul, on August 17, 2021, Taliban spokesman Zabihullah Mujahid sought to reassure Afghans and the international community that the group's return to power would not mean a reversal of women's rights.Addressing the first press conference after the takeover, he said women would be allowed to work, study and participate in society, provided they followed the Taliban's interpretation of Islamic law. He also said the group would not discriminate against women.In a separate interview with Sky News on the same day, Taliban spokesman Suhail Shaheen made an explicit promise that Afghan women would be allowed to pursue education up to university level and continue working. He said the group was committed to women's rights, education, employment and freedom of speech under its interpretation of Islamic rules.However, the assurances were followed by a series of restrictions that progressively excluded women from education, employment and public life.In September 2021, when secondary schools reopened, boys were allowed to return to classrooms while most girls were kept at home.From school closures to a wider crackdown on women's rightsThe first major reversal came on March 23, 2022, when the Taliban abruptly cancelled the reopening of secondary schools for girls, despite earlier indications that they would be allowed to resume classes.Girls who had arrived expecting to return to school were sent home, with the authorities saying reopening would remain suspended until a decision was made on uniforms in accordance with their interpretation of Islamic law. The restriction effectively barred girls from formal education beyond Grade 6.The restrictions subsequently extended to women's employment and freedom of movement. In December 2022, the Taliban barred Afghan women from working with national and international non-governmental organisations (NGOs), while also announcing a ban on women's attendance at public and private universities.In April 2023, the prohibition on women's employment was extended to Afghan women working for the United Nations in the country.Five years after the Taliban takeover, restrictions on Afghan women have extended far beyond education, affecting their employment, freedom of movement, access to healthcare and participation in public life.According to UN Women's assessment published on August 12, 2026, Taliban authorities have issued more than 100 decrees affecting women and girls since returning to power. The agency found that more than half of women surveyed leave their homes only once or twice a month, while nearly three-quarters feel unsafe going out without a male guardian.The restrictions have also affected women's access to healthcare. Shortages of female health workers, restrictions on women's employment in the health sector and limitations on their movement have made it harder for many to access medical services. UN Women estimated Afghanistan's maternal mortality rate at 638 deaths per 100,000 live births in 2024.The Taliban's August 2024 Law on the Promotion of Virtue and Prevention of Vice further formalised restrictions on women's public conduct, clothing and movement. The law also imposed restrictions on women's voices being heard in public.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: A Montana couple put a home in the wife's name before marrying in 2023, though the husband funded nearly $955,000 in purchase and improvements; after their split, the state Supreme Court upheld awarding him the property
articles.summary: A Montana couple who put a home in the wife’s name before marrying in 2023 have seen the state Supreme Court uphold a decision awarding the property to
articles.body: A Montana couple who put a home in the wife’s name before marrying in 2023 have seen the state Supreme Court uphold a decision awarding the property to the husband after their split. The court found that the husband had paid almost $955,000 for the purchase costs and improvements, and therefore had a strong case for treating the home as his, even though the title was in his wife’s name. The case illustrates that judges don't just look at whose name is on a deed when deciding who gets what in a divorce. In this instance, the Montana Supreme Court concluded that the husband’s financial contributions and the circumstances surrounding the purchase justified awarding him the home. Read more about it here, as per report on Justia U.S. Law:The home and the marriageThe couple bought the home before marrying in 2023, but the title was placed in the wife’s name. Despite this, the husband provided nearly $955,000 toward the purchase and later improvements to the property. When the relationship ended, the question became who should keep the home. The wife argued that the property was hers because it was titled in her name, while the husband pointed to the money he had put into it.The trial court ruled for the husband and awarded him the property. The wife appealed, but the Montana Supreme Court upheld the decision, finding that the evidence supported the lower court’s ruling.Why the court ruled in his favourUnder Montana law, courts are allowed to look beyond the title when dividing property in a divorce. The court looked at the whole picture, including who paid for the house and who contributed to its maintenance and improvement. The husband’s contribution of nearly $955,000 played an important part in the decision. The court held that the amount of money he put into the home was a clear indication that he intended it to be his, regardless of whether the title said otherwise.The court also looked at the timing of the purchase and what the couple’s plans were at the time. Since the home was bought before the marriage and the husband had funded most of it, the court saw little reason to treat it as marital property subject to equal division.What this means for couplesFor couples buying property before they get married, the case reminds them that title alone doesn't always determine ownership in a divorce. Courts will consider who paid for the property, who maintained it and what the parties intended at the time of purchase. This is especially true when one person puts up most of the cash, but the other has his name on the title. Disputes like this can get complicated and costly without clear documentation or a written agreement.For anyone in a similar situation, the lesson is to keep records of payments and improvements. These can make a significant difference if the relationship ends and the property becomes part of a divorce case.A costly outcomeThe wife’s attempt to keep the home based on the title failed, and the property was awarded to the husband. The judgement emphasises the principle of looking at the substance, rather than the form, of a transaction. or the husband, that his money investment is acknowledged and secured. For the wife, it is a reminder that title does not mean ownership if the other party can prove a greater contribution and intent.This case also serves to emphasise the necessity of a clear agreement when a couple purchases property together.You can define each person’s rights either through a written contract or a co-ownership arrangement to help prevent disputes later on.The greater lessonMontana’s Supreme Court has stated that in divorce cases, the courts will look beyond formal titles to determine property ownership. This approach can protect people who have invested heavily in a home but do not hold the deed.For anyone buying property with a partner, the case is a call to be clear about ownership from the start. Whether through a written agreement or a joint title, spelling out each person’s rights can save time, money and stress if the relationship ends.The $955,000 the husband put into the home was central to the court’s decision. Without that level of contribution, the outcome might have been different, but the evidence made a strong case that the property was meant to be his.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: Oasis star Noel Gallagher wins approval to renovate his £11.5 million Grade II-listed London mansion; plans include a sauna, cinema room and basement bar
articles.summary: Noel Gallagher's plans for his new London home are beginning to take shape, although bringing the historic property up to his requirements has involved
articles.body: Noel Gallagher's plans for his new London home are beginning to take shape, although bringing the historic property up to his requirements has involved dealing with a number of problems. According to The Standard UK, the Oasis guitarist, who bought the seven-bedroom residence for £11.5 million last year, is preparing an extensive programme of repairs and improvements to the Grade II-listed building. The work comes after issues were identified with parts of the property, including its roof, internal structure and lower-level walls. Alongside addressing the defects, Gallagher wants to introduce several modern features, among them a private gym, sauna, cinema room and basement bar.Inside Noel Gallagher's £11.5 million London propertyAccording to Daily Mail, Gallagher's new residence is a five-storey property in north London with a history of its own. The Grade II-listed building was once divided into separate flats before a previous owner brought the units together to create a single family home. Its layout and historic features mean that any substantial renovation needs to be considered within the restrictions that apply to listed properties.The purchase gave the musician a seven-bedroom home, but the building has not been without its maintenance concerns. Planning documents submitted to Westminster City Council refer to several defects that need attention, including structural movement and problems affecting different parts of the building.The Standard UK reported that the property is now at the centre of a renovation programme intended to address those issues while making the interiors more suitable for modern residential use.Roof leaks and rising damp add to renovation workThe proposed work follows the identification of water-related damage and deterioration in the building's fabric. Gallagher's renovation plans include tackling water entering through the roof, damp affecting the lower floors and sections of the roof covering that have deteriorated over time.The planning papers also refer to earlier alterations that are considered unsuitable for the historic character of the house. Structural movement is another issue mentioned in the council documents, adding to the list of matters that need to be addressed during the restoration.A gym, sauna and cinema room among the planned additionsAlongside the repair work, Gallagher has outlined a number of changes to the property's facilities. The proposed additions include a gym, a sauna, a private cinema room and a bar in the basement.The plans also involve removing existing fixtures and fittings from the rooms as the interiors are reworked. An adjoining building is expected to be converted into a one-bedroom guest suite, providing separate accommodation within the wider property.The proposed entertainment facilities would add to the home's existing residential space, while the guest accommodation would make use of a connected building. The project therefore involves both the main house and the adjoining structure.Gallagher’s architects seek to preserve mansion’s historic characterThe Grade II listing places limits on the changes that can be made to the property. Gallagher has received permission for some elements of the renovation, but other proposals still require the relevant approval.Among the changes awaiting consideration are the replacement of existing windows with double-glazed sash windows, as well as alterations to the roof and doors of the rear extension. These details are particularly important because changes to the appearance and historic fabric of a listed building are subject to additional planning controls.The architectural team has presented the proposed work as a programme of necessary repairs and carefully considered upgrades rather than a major redesign. The planning documents describe an approach that favours taking materials apart carefully instead of demolishing sections unnecessarily. Materials that cannot be reused are intended to be sorted for recycling wherever possible.How the renovation aims to improve energy efficiencyThe proposals also address the property's environmental performance. The planned improvements include slim-profile double glazing designed for conservation settings, better draught-proofing and additional insulation in the roof.More efficient building services and durable natural materials also feature in the architectural plans. These measures are intended to improve the home's energy performance without making unnecessary changes to its historic structure.The architects have argued that repairing and upgrading the existing building is a more appropriate approach than replacing large sections of it. Their planning statement says the work is limited to maintaining and renewing defective parts of the building, removing later internal alterations and updating services through existing routes.They have also maintained that the proposals will not change the character or appearance of the listed property or interfere with features of particular architectural or historic interest.Noel Gallagher's previous homes in north LondonThis is not Gallagher's first high-profile residential property in north London. During his marriage to his first wife, Meg Matthews, he lived at a Belsize Park house that became known as Supernova Heights, a name inspired by Oasis's song Champagne Supernova.Gallagher later married Sara McDonald, with whom he spent more than a decade before their divorce was finalised in 2023, after 12 years of marriage.His latest property purchase comes after another major period in the musician's career. The Oasis reunion tour in 2025 brought Noel and his younger brother Liam Gallagher back on stage together, with performances attracting audiences across several countries.You use AI every day. articles.title: Florida's giant Burmese pythons are not just eating wildlife; they may be spreading seeds, transforming the Everglades in an unexpected way
articles.summary: Florida's Everglades is facing an ecological challenge from one of its most notorious invasive predators, the giant Burmese python.
articles.body: Florida's Everglades is facing an ecological challenge from one of its most notorious invasive predators, the giant Burmese python. The snakes have devastated populations of native mammals and disrupted the delicate balance of the wetland ecosystem. However, scientists have uncovered another, less obvious way these reptiles may be influencing the landscape. New research suggests that Burmese pythons could be helping plants spread by transporting seeds after consuming fruit-eating birds and mammals. Researchers identified 25 different seed types in the digestive tracts of the snakes, revealing that their ecological influence extends beyond hunting and feeding. This means the pythons could unintentionally act as seed carriers, transporting seeds from one location to another through their prey. Some seeds can even survive the digestive process and remain capable of germinating, potentially allowing plants to grow in new areas of the Everglades. The discovery offers a surprising insight into how an invasive predator can alter an ecosystem through unexpected biological interactions.Scientists found 25 types of seeds inside Burmese pythonsThe findings come from a study published in the Journal of Zoology, titled Double agents: Invasive Burmese pythons (Python bivittatus) and Argentine black and white tegus (Salvator merianae) as potential seed dispersers in South Florida. The research involved scientists from the University of Florida, the US Geological Survey and the Conservancy of Southwest Florida.Researchers examined digestive tract samples collected from invasive Burmese pythons in South Florida and identified 25 different seed types. These included seeds from native plants such as cabbage palm and creeping cucumber.The discovery suggests that pythons can unintentionally transport seeds after consuming birds and mammals that have previously eaten fruits. The seeds remain inside the snakes' digestive systems and may eventually be deposited at different locations.This process is known as secondary seed dispersal. Unlike animals that directly consume fruits and distribute their seeds, Burmese pythons can move seeds indirectly by eating animals that already carry them.Nearly 40% of some seeds survived the digestive processOne of the more significant findings involved cabbage palm seeds, which showed an ability to survive passage through a python's digestive system.Germination experiments found that nearly 40% of these seeds survived digestion and subsequently sprouted. This suggests that the snakes may transport viable seeds across different parts of the Everglades rather than simply destroying them during digestion.Seed survival is an important factor in determining whether an animal can contribute to plant dispersal. If seeds remain capable of germinating after passing through a predator's digestive tract, they may establish themselves in locations far from the original fruit-bearing plants.The findings also raise questions about which plant species could benefit from this unusual form of transportation. Both native and invasive plants could potentially be affected, depending on which seeds are carried and where they are deposited.Burmese pythons have already devastated Everglades wildlifeBurmese pythons are native to Southeast Asia but have become established across South Florida, particularly in the Greater Everglades ecosystem. Their presence is considered a major threat to native wildlife because of their size, appetite and ability to hunt a wide variety of animals.The snakes prey on mammals and birds, including raccoons, rabbits, opossums and other native species. Their expansion has contributed to substantial declines in several mammal populations across parts of the Everglades.These animals also perform important ecological functions, including seed dispersal. By consuming fruits and carrying seeds to different locations, fruit-eating mammals and birds help maintain plant populations and vegetation diversity.As python populations expand and native animal communities change, the movement of seeds across the ecosystem may also be affected. The snakes' unexpected role as secondary seed carriers adds another layer to an already complicated ecological relationship.Researchers also studied invasive tegu lizardsThe research examined another invasive reptile in South Florida: the Argentine black and white tegu (Salvator merianae).Unlike Burmese pythons, which primarily act as predators, tegus are omnivorous reptiles that directly consume fruits and seeds. Researchers identified 73 different seed types in tegu samples, compared with 25 in Burmese pythons.Together, the two reptiles were associated with seeds belonging to 38 plant families, including native, endangered and invasive species.The researchers also used a binary interaction network to examine how these reptiles interact with different plant species and potentially become integrated into existing seed-dispersal networks.Their findings suggest that invasive reptiles can influence plant distribution through multiple pathways, from directly eating fruits to consuming animals that have already ingested seeds.An unexpected dimension of invasive speciesThe study highlights how invasive animals can influence ecosystems through interactions that are not immediately visible. Burmese pythons are primarily recognised for their impact on native wildlife, but their feeding habits may also affect the movement of plant seeds.The researchers' findings point to the possibility that invasive reptiles could become part of the ecological networks they initially disrupt. Their presence may influence which plants spread, how seeds move and how vegetation patterns develop across the Greater Everglades.The research was published in the February 2026 issue of the Journal of Zoology, with the study first appearing online on November 9, 2025.You use AI every day. articles.title: Metallica drummer Lars Ulrich bought two adjoining San Francisco mansions from Salesforce founder Marc Benioff for $36 million; nearly a decade later, he sold both for nearly $68 million
articles.summary: Metallica drummer Lars Ulrich has sold two adjoining mansions in San Francisco for nearly $68 million, almost doubling the amount he paid for the
articles.body: Metallica drummer Lars Ulrich has sold two adjoining mansions in San Francisco for nearly $68 million, almost doubling the amount he paid for the properties from Salesforce founder Marc Benioff nearly a decade earlier. The homes, located in the city's affluent Presidio Heights neighbourhood, were sold on the same day in separate transactions, according to The San Francisco Standard. The sale represents one of the city's biggest residential property deals and forms part of a wider real estate exit by Ulrich, who has also sold a substantial parcel of land in neighbouring Marin County.Lars Ulrich's San Francisco mansions nearly doubled in valueThe San Francisco Standard reported that Ulrich was the owner behind 2 trusts that sold the adjoining properties for almost $68 million. Although the houses changed hands separately, their combined sale would rank as the second-largest private residential transaction in San Francisco history if treated as a single deal.The figure would place the transaction behind Laurene Powell Jobs' $71 million purchase on Billionaire's Row in 2024. The drummer purchased the properties from Benioff, his longtime friend, through two separate transactions. The combined original purchase price was $36 million, making the latest sale a significant financial gain for Ulrich after years of ownership.According to The San Francisco Standard, the properties were sold last week, with the two trusts transferring ownership on the same day. Their adjoining layouts and substantial sizes made them a particularly notable combination in the city's luxury housing market.What made the two Presidio Heights properties distinctiveThe larger residence stands at 3277 Pacific Avenue and measures approximately 16,000 square feet. Ulrich purchased it in May 2017 for $30 million through a trust connected to WG & S, a family office firm, as detailed by The San Francisco Standard.The second property, at 3230 Jackson Street, is considerably smaller, with around 6,000 square feet of living space. It was acquired in October 2018 for $6 million through a separate trust overseen by entertainment attorney Edwin McPherson.Together, the homes offer approximately 22,000 square feet of residential space. Their neighbouring backyards appear to connect the properties, creating an arrangement for two separately owned houses in the prestigious neighbourhood.The San Francisco Standard reported that the larger Pacific Avenue estate was designed by architect Willis Polk in 1913. Its architecture drew inspiration from Italian palazzos, giving the mansion a distinctive historic character.The property underwent a major renovation during the 1990s for Mickey Drexler, the former chief executive of Gap and J.Crew. Designer Thierry Despont was responsible for the interiors, which incorporated a French-North African aesthetic and included an indoor swimming pool on a lower level.Who owned the mansions before Lars UlrichThe properties had already passed through several prominent owners before Ulrich acquired them. Benioff purchased the Jackson Street residence in 2000 for $7.5 million, according to The San Francisco Standard. 5 years later, he bought the larger Pacific Avenue mansion from his neighbour Drexler for $25 million.Benioff's ownership of both homes preceded their eventual transfer to Ulrich. The Salesforce founder sold the properties to the drummer in separate deals, with the Pacific Avenue estate changing hands in 2017 and the Jackson Street residence following in 2018.The transactions were conducted through trusts rather than directly in Ulrich's name. The San Francisco Standard identified the larger property's purchasing trust as being connected to WG & S, while the smaller home's trust was managed by McPherson.The identities of the latest buyers have not been officially confirmed. AXS TV reported that records showed the properties were acquired by trusts controlled by Robert Joseph St. Aubin, whose representation of trusts connected to Airbnb chief executive Brian Chesky was referenced in a 2020 Securities and Exchange Commission filing. However, neither Chesky nor anyone connected to him has been confirmed as the actual buyer.Ulrich's wider Bay Area property salesThe San Francisco mansions were not the only significant property Ulrich sold during the period. The Metallica drummer also parted with a 161-acre parcel atop King Mountain in Marin County for $16 million, bringing the combined value of his recent Bay Area property sales to approximately $84 million.The San Francisco Standard reported that the Marin property was purchased by the Marin Open Space Trust, which intends to make it accessible to the public. The acquisition was funded through a grant from the Shelby Cullom Davis Charitable Fund.The land sits near Kentfield and offers views of Mount Tamalpais and the surrounding landscape. Its sale also brings an end to Ulrich's long-running plans to develop a private compound on the site.The property had previously been marketed for around $40 million in 2015, with later asking prices falling considerably. Its eventual sale to a conservation organisation instead means the land is expected to become a public recreational resource.The San Francisco Standard also reported that Ulrich had previously sold a Tiburon property for $10.3 million in 2020. That home had been purchased in the early 1990s and later placed into a trust.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? Build Your Legacy with TOI Homes.

articles.title: Miami woman moves into a new apartment with her 2 kids. 2 weeks later, she allegedly breaks into her neighbor’s home and hauls their furniture outside
articles.summary: A Miami couple came home from work last week to find their furniture dumped in their apartment complex’s rear common area. Police accuse their neighbor, 42-y...
articles.body:
A Miami couple came home from work last week to find their furniture dumped in their apartment complex's rear common area. Police accuse their neighbor, 42-year-old Nicole Bottiglieri-Vega, of breaking in, according to Law & Crime . She faces charges of third-degree grand theft, contributing to the delinquency or dependency of a child, criminal mischief, and resisting an officer without violence.

The property manager reviewed surveillance footage and saw Bottiglieri-Vega, who wore a long dress, leave her apartment with two children and allegedly force open the couple's back door . Police say one child helped carry items out, and a neighbor's Ring camera reportedly backed up the footage. The manager recognized her as a tenant who had moved in two weeks earlier.

Officers knocked on Bottiglieri-Vega's door and rear windows, but she reportedly refused to respond. As children were inside, police contacted the Florida Department of Children and Families, though its investigator also could not reach her that evening.

Police say she slipped out of her handcuffs at the station

Officers returned the next afternoon alongside child welfare workers, and a police sergeant reportedly heard screaming and spotted blood near the door. Police forced their way into the apartment and found Bottiglieri-Vega inside a bedroom. She allegedly refused commands and pulled away while officers handcuffed her, though they managed to take her into custody.

Police took Bottiglieri-Vega to the department's North Station and placed her in a holding cell. Officers say she slipped out of her handcuffs and approached the cell door leading into the main facility before an officer recuffed her. Detectives later tried to interview her, but the session ended as she reportedly refused to answer questions.

A witness also told officers that Bottiglieri-Vega frequently used narcotics, according to the arrest report. The witness claimed to have seen her smoking crack cocaine and leaving glass pipes and small plastic bags around the premises. However, those claims have not been independently verified, and none of the four charges involve drugs.

The grand theft charge alone could mean years in prison

Under Florida law , third-degree grand theft covers property valued at $750 or more but less than $20,000. The state classifies it as a third-degree felony, which could carry up to five years in prison and a $5,000 fine on conviction. However, police have not publicly said what value they placed on the couple's damaged and moved belongings.

Contributing to the delinquency or dependency of a child is a first-degree misdemeanor under section 827.04 of the Florida Statutes , punishable by up to one year in jail. As children were involved, DCF runs its own process, and a Florida Senate analysis notes that protective investigations must begin immediately or within 24 hours, depending on the allegation.

Bottiglieri-Vega was booked into the Turner Guilford Knight Correctional Center with bond reportedly set at more than $11,000, and her next court date was not immediately listed.

articles.title: An Arizona couple built three businesses during their marriage, including a car-rental venture; during their divorce, the husband disputed a $305,800 business valuation and $95,000 in alleged loans, but an appeals court upheld the lower court’s ruling
articles.summary: An Arizona couple built three businesses during their marriage, including a car-rental venture; during their divorce, the husband disputed a $305,800
articles.body: An Arizona couple built three businesses during their marriage, including a car-rental venture; during their divorce, the husband disputed a $305,800 business valuation and $95,000 in alleged loans, but an appeals court upheld the lower court’s rulingAn Arizona appeals court has upheld a divorce ruling that split a couple’s three businesses and refused to share $95,000 in loans the husband said were marital debt. The court found the husband’s loan papers lacked credibility, and it accepted a $305,800 valuation of one company even though he refused to give the expert his financial records. The decision, issued October 30, 2026, is a non-precedential memorandum, so it does not set a rule for other cases.A marriage, three business and money fights The Arizona couple married in September 2016. Over the next several years, they built three businesses together: a company that took the couple’s name, a car-rental business run through the Turo platform, and a second company under the wife’s name. When the marriage ended, they had to decide who got what.In December 2023, the wife filed for divorce and served the husband a week later. The Maricopa County Superior Court held a one-day trial to split the couple’s debts, property, and businesses. The husband later appealed, representing himself.The husband refused to provide financial records After filing the appeal, the court appointed an expert, chosen by both spouses, to value the first company. The expert asked the husband for payroll records and tax forms, however, he refused to hand them over. The expert still reached a value of $305,800, and the trial court accepted it.The husband wasn’t happy with the valuation. He argued that the business had no hard assets and that the expert focused too much on one unusually profitable year. He also said the expert was biased. The appeals court disagreed. It said the expert explained his work and listed the documents he used. A zero value, the court noted, would ignore goodwill, which can carry real money in a business.Though the Turo business was jointly owned, the husband ran it. He bought several cars with loans, and the amounts owed were more than the cars were worth. He also claimed tax deductions for depreciating the cars, and kept the rental profits.The husband failed to disclose profits or tax gains during the case. The cars were worth less than what was owed, and that difference is called negative equity. The court split the negative equity. It gave the husband the cars, the profits he had taken, and the tax benefits. The wife was responsible for half the gap, minus an offset for what the husband owed her from other property. The appeals court said the facts supported this approach.The couple had taken a second mortgage to start the second company. By the time of the divorce, nobody argued that the business was worth anything. The husband claimed the wife wasted marital money. She testified that he agreed to the loan and that the money went to credit card debt, home repairs, and a horse structure next to the house.Eventually, the husband agreed to give the business to the wife with no payment to him, even though he had taken the opposite position for most of the case. The court awarded it to her. His claims about money being wasted failed because he never testified and his spreadsheets did not show how the wife had wasted money.The husband asked to split the loans equallyThe husband requested the court to split three personal loans equally: $80,000 from his parents, $10,000 from one friend, and $5,000 from another. Under Arizona law, debt taken on during a marriage is usually shared. He gave the court documents only one month before trial, and they had no notarization. The wife said she had no idea about the loans and believed he made the papers for the trial. The judge did not find the documents credible and refused to split the debt. As a result, all the four arguments raised by the husband were rejected by the Arizona Court of Appeals. The court said it would not reweigh the evidence or second-guess the trial judge’s view of who was telling the truth. The wife asked for her attorneys’ fees, but the court denied that request. The decision was issued on October 30, 2026. It is a memorandum decision, which means it is not binding precedent in other cases.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: In 2025, Paris Jackson challenged $625,000 in legal bonuses from Michael Jackson's estate; now she seeks a $600 million family trust transfer
articles.summary: In 2025, Paris Jackson challenged $625,000 in additional legal payments made from her late father Michael Jackson’s estate.
articles.body: In 2025, Paris Jackson challenged $625,000 in additional legal payments made from her late father Michael Jackson’s estate. Now, she is taking another step in questioning how his multibillion-dollar fortune is being managed. The 28-year-old has asked a Los Angeles court to order the transfer of $600 million into the Michael Jackson Family Trust, which is intended to benefit her and her brothers. According to The Los Angeles Times, the petition raises questions about years of delayed trust funding, estate finances and when the singer’s three children will receive the financial benefits their father intended for them.Paris Jackson seeks $600 million transfer after challenging estate paymentsParis Jackson's latest petition asks a Los Angeles court to direct the remaining executor of her father's estate to transfer $600 million into the Michael Jackson Family Trust. The request is intended to benefit all three children, Paris, Prince and Bigi, rather than provide the entire amount to her personally.According to The Los Angeles Times, the filing argues that the family trust has remained without the funding it was supposed to receive, despite the estate's considerable financial growth since the singer's death in 2009. Paris is seeking an initial transfer of $600 million, although she has also asked the judge to determine another appropriate amount if necessary.The request follows her earlier objections to the way the estate's finances have been handled. Paris has questioned the additional payments made to outside legal firms, the timing of financial distributions and the delay in moving money into the children's trust.What happened in Paris Jackson's $625,000 legal-fee dispute in 2025The earlier disagreement concerned $625,000 in additional bonus payments authorised by estate executors John Branca and John McClain for three outside law firms representing Michael Jackson's estate during the second half of 2018.In June 2025, Paris objected when the executors sought court approval for attorney compensation and expenses relating to that period. She argued that the additional payments had not been sufficiently explained and questioned whether there was adequate justification for the amounts involved. The matter eventually came before Los Angeles Superior Court Judge Mitchell L. Beckloff. During an evidentiary hearing, Branca testified that 2018 had been a particularly successful year for the estate because of several business transactions.The judge, however, concluded that the information presented did not establish that the bonus payments were reasonable. In 2026, Beckloff ruled against approving the $625,000 and ordered the money returned to the estate. Paris was also found entitled to reasonable attorneys' fees.The ruling did not establish that Branca or McClain had personally received the disputed payments. Their legal representatives later clarified that the money had gone to outside law firms and that the executors had not paid themselves those bonuses.Why Michael Jackson's three children are waiting for their family trustMichael Jackson died on June 25, 2009, aged 50, leaving behind three children. Prince and Paris were born during his marriage to Debbie Rowe, while his youngest son, Bigi, formerly known as Blanket, was born through a surrogate.According to the trust arrangements described in Paris's court filing, the children were expected to begin receiving income from their respective trust interests at 21, followed by distributions from the principal at 30, 35 and 40.Prince is now 29, Paris is 28 and Bigi is 24. Paris argues that the arrangements have not been implemented as intended because the family trust has not received the funding necessary to carry them out.Her filing also points to developments in 2011, when the executors reportedly indicated that they intended to approach the court about beginning the funding process. Paris maintains that the promised application was never made, leaving the beneficiaries waiting for years.How Michael Jackson's estate grew into a multibillion-dollar fortuneMichael Jackson's estate has continued to generate revenue from his music and other business interests since his death in 2009. Executors John Branca and John McClain oversaw deals involving his music catalogue, publishing rights and other assets, several of which brought in substantial sums.In 2018, the estate sold its stake in EMI Music Publishing for approximately $287.5 million. Two years later, Neverland Ranch, Jackson's former California home, was sold for around $22 million, according to the Los Angeles Times.The estate reached another major agreement with Sony in 2023, involving Jackson's music and intellectual property. The value of the estate has since become a central point in the dispute over how much money should be transferred to the family trust.In Paris's court filing, her legal team cites earlier valuations by the executors that placed the estate's worth between $2 billion and $3 billion. The filing also points to an estate accounting showing approximately $850 million in cash and cash-equivalent assets as of December 2024.IRS dispute remains an obstacle to funding the family trustOne of the issues affecting the estate is its long-running dispute with the Internal Revenue Service (IRS). The tax authority previously challenged the estate's valuation of Michael Jackson's assets and sought approximately $700 million in taxes and penalties.In a statement to PEOPLE, representatives of the estate said that several outstanding legal matters needed to be settled before the family trust could be fully funded. They also rejected the suggestion that the executors had deliberately withheld money from the children or prevented them from receiving their intended benefits.John Branca becomes sole executor after John McClain's deathBranca and music executive John McClain were appointed co-executors following Michael Jackson's death in 2009. They were responsible for managing the singer's financial affairs, negotiating commercial agreements and overseeing the development of his estate.McClain died in May 2026, leaving Branca as the remaining executor. His departure has added another dimension to the questions surrounding the estate's administration. Paris's latest petition focuses on the remaining executor's responsibility for transferring money into the family trust and providing beneficiaries with greater clarity about the estate's financial decisions.The earlier dispute over the $625,000 payments also forms part of this wider disagreement. Paris has repeatedly questioned the additional compensation authorised for outside advisers and the way financial decisions have been presented to the court.The estate's representatives, meanwhile, have defended the executors' record, pointing to the substantial increase in the estate's value since 2009 and the wealth created for Michael Jackson's beneficiaries.Court to consider Paris Jackson's $600 million requestParis is now asking the Los Angeles court to consider an initial transfer of $600 million into the family trust before all outstanding matters involving the estate have been resolved. She has left room for the judge to determine a different amount if the requested figure is not considered appropriate.The court will now have to consider both positions as it examines the request. Until a decision is made, the $600 million remains a proposed transfer for the benefit of Michael Jackson's three children.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: US held secret talks with Iran to deport its nationals even as war raged, court filings show
articles.summary: US' Donald Trump administration held secret talks with Iranian officials over the deportation of Iranian nationals even as the war between the United
articles.body: US' Donald Trump administration held secret talks with Iranian officials over the deportation of Iranian nationals even as the war between the United States and Iran continued, newly unsealed court documents have revealed.According to news agency AP, filings show that the US government was still exploring arrangements to remove Iranians through an unnamed third country as recently as mid-October.The documents, unsealed on Thursday, also reveal that US immigration officials maintained contact with Iranian authorities during the conflict to submit travel documents and discuss “possible avenues for removal”.In an October 15 hearing, US District Judge Ana Reyes questioned the government's decision to pursue deportations to a country that the US President had described as an enemy.“We are at war with a country where the President of the United States has said, as recently as two or three days ago, if not yesterday, that it is essentially lawless... A country that is an enemy of the United States, according to the current president. A country that, according to our president, murdered tens of thousands of protestors,” Reyes said, according to the hearing transcript quoted by AP.The judge further questioned the risks faced by Iranian nationals if they were returned to the country.“And what you're telling me is that the United States of America is going to send individuals back to that region, facing what you and I and everyone who would ever look at this would know would be, at a minimum, a serious threat of certain death.”Responding to the judge, Justice Department attorney Dimitar Georgiev-Remmel defended the administration's position.“Yes, your honour,” he said. “The government is executing lawful orders of removal.”The judge subsequently directed the government to provide the court with 24-hour notice of any finalised plans to deport Iranians to Iran or another country. The administration was also ordered to give five days' written notice before carrying out any such deportation.The revelations have emerged from an ongoing lawsuit alleging that US immigration agencies shared confidential information about Iranian asylum seekers with the Iranian government, potentially exposing them to persecution. The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) has denied sharing asylum application records with Tehran.Hundreds of emails exchanged between US immigration officials reportedly detail coordination between the two governments to arrange the return of more than 100 Iranians on three immigration flights in September and December 2025 and January 2026.Deportations to Iran have historically been rare because Washington and Tehran lack diplomatic relations and returnees could face persecution.However, the Trump administration has pursued removals to countries with which the US has limited diplomatic cooperation, including El Salvador, Costa Rica and Panama. In June, an Iranian woman was among two dozen migrants deported to the Central African Republic.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: A teenage boy Jim Bishop spent over 50 years building Colorado’s 160-foot Bishop Castle by hand without formal training; he died aged 80 in 2024, and today, son Dan maintains the landmark
articles.summary: A teenage boy with no formal training in construction set out to build a small stone cottage in the mountains of southern Colorado.
articles.body: A teenage boy with no formal training in construction set out to build a small stone cottage in the mountains of southern Colorado. More than five decades later, that modest project had transformed into a 16-storey, 160-foot-tall medieval-style castle, complete with towers, bridges, stained-glass windows and even a fire-breathing dragon.The man behind this extraordinary creation was Jim Bishop, whose ambitious undertaking is widely regarded as one of the largest one-man construction projects in the world. Known as Bishop Castle, the sprawling structure was built largely by Bishop himself, without formal architectural or engineering training.Bishop died in November 2024, aged 80. Today, his son Dan looks after the castle and continues to welcome visitors to the unusual landmark, which remains open to the public and operates on donations.From a paper route to a mountain propertyBishop’s remarkable journey began in 1959, when he was just 15. He had saved money from delivering newspapers, mowing lawns and doing odd jobs, along with earnings from working at his father’s ornamental ironworks. He used his savings to put down $500 towards a 2.5-acre piece of forested land in the mountains of southern Colorado. The property cost $2,500, which he paid off over the next 10 years.Because he was underage, his parents had to sign the paperwork on his behalf. After buying the land, Bishop reportedly cycled 48 miles into the mountains to see what he had purchased.He had already fallen out with school following a disagreement with an English teacher and eventually dropped out of high school. Instead of pursuing formal education, he learned ironwork and masonry through practical experience. His grandfather, a Navy tinsmith, taught him some of the skills involved in working with metal.In 1969, Bishop and his father began constructing a small stone cottage on the property. The original idea was to create a weekend retreat in the mountains. But as the structure began attracting attention from motorists travelling along Highway 165, people started asking whether he was building a castle. Some even mocked the idea.That reaction eventually became the inspiration for something much bigger.Recalling the moment his grandfather asked Jim what he was doing while digging at the property, Dan said his father replied, “The people want a castle. I'm going to build one. I'm expanding.”According to Dan, the idea of building a castle had taken hold of his father's imagination, and he decided to pursue it.A cottage that became a castleBishop’s son recalls that his father initially spent about three years building the rock cottage. He then worked on the beginnings of a castle for nearly a decade, with friends occasionally offering to help but rarely turning up. Eventually, the project became a one-man undertaking.The original cottage gradually evolved into an extraordinary structure featuring multiple towers, stone arches, buttresses, wrought-iron bridges, battlements, stained-glass windows and a grand hall. One of its most striking features is a metal dragon designed to breathe fire.The tallest tower rises approximately 160 feet above the ground, with around 15 feet of its foundation buried down to bedrock. According to Dan, his father built much of the structure by relying on his own calculations, instinct and practical understanding of balance rather than architectural drawings.Bishop reportedly carried out much of the heavy work himself. He would collect rocks from nearby creek beds using a half-ton truck, bring them back to the property and move them into position using a system of pulleys and baskets. Dan says his father handled each rock an average of seven times before it reached its final position.Explaining his father's approach to construction, Dan recalled a line Jim often used: “Engineering without money is ingenuity.” He said his father had plenty of the latter, despite having no formal engineering education.The work was largely done during the summer months. During winter, Bishop returned to his ornamental ironwork business to earn money for his living expenses and finance the next phase of construction. He would then devote much of June, July and August to building the castle.The fire-breathing dragon and unconventional engineeringThe castle is filled with unusual architectural features that reflect Bishop’s imagination. Among them is a metal dragon whose mouth can release enormous flames. Dan explained during a tour of the property that his father initially installed a hot-air balloon burner in the dragon, which produced a flame of about five feet. The current mechanism is considerably more powerful.The structure also contains elaborate stone arches, metal frameworks, towers and unfinished projects, including an elevator and an inclined escalator. Bishop had envisioned the latter as a way to help visitors in wheelchairs access parts of the castle.His son explained that many of these ideas existed primarily in his father’s imagination. Bishop rarely drew detailed plans and often came up with new additions as he went along. He took inspiration from photographs of Germany’s Neuschwanstein Castle, the work of Spanish architect Antoni Gaudí and other architectural references he encountered in magazines.Despite the scale of the undertaking, Bishop continued to build without conventional construction machinery or formal engineering assistance. Electricity did not reach the property until 1993.Clashes with authorities and a monument to freedomThe project also brought Bishop into conflict with local authorities. At one point, officials told him that he needed building permits and could not continue constructing beyond a certain height. According to Dan, his father challenged the restrictions and presented an argument based on the legal doctrine of laches at a local board meeting.Bishop saw the castle as a symbol of individual freedom and the possibilities of determination. His son described it as a monument to what a person could accomplish with limited resources, provided they had the will and desire to keep going.Speaking about his father's philosophy, Dan said, “This place is a monument to freedom. What you can do without much if you have the will and desire and you don't let them stop you.”Jim also had a strong sense of spirituality, although Dan said he was not particularly religious. His father often said that “with these two hands and the help of God” he had built Bishop Castle. Bishop did not charge admission, and visitors were encouraged to contribute donations instead. The family continues to follow that approach.His son continues the legacyAfter Jim Bishop’s death in November 2024, his son Dan took on the responsibility of looking after the castle.
